content: Brad Cohen is a motivational speaker, an award-winning teacher, and an author. He has a severe case of Tourette syndrome, which he describes in his book, Front of the Class: How Tourette Syndrome Made Me the Teacher I Never Had. During his childhood, he was often misunderstood and accused of being a troublemaker in school due to his tics, and he was unfairly punished by his teachers. This experience inspired him to become the teacher that he never had. After earning his teaching certificate, he faced rejection from 24 elementary schools before finally being hired at Mountain View Elementary School in Cobb County, Georgia. As a new teacher, he was recognized for his excellence and won the Teacher of the Year Award for the state of Georgia. On June 25, 2006, Brad Cohen married Nancy Lazarus from Charleston, South Carolina. Brad grew up in St. Louis, Missouri, in a Jewish family. His parents divorced during his early childhood. While his mother was compassionate and supportive, his father struggled to understand Tourette syndrome. His father often became frustrated with Brad’s vocal and physical tics, leading to frequent yelling. When his father moved away, their relationship became distant. During his school years, Brad’s teachers misunderstood his condition, interpreting his tics as disruptive behavior. This experience deeply affected him and motivated him to become a teacher who would focus on students' strengths rather than their weaknesses. In eighth grade, his principal allowed him to address the school about his Tourette syndrome, which marked the beginning of his journey as a public speaker. Over time, he gained confidence and honed his speaking skills by sharing his story with others. Brad attended Bradley University in Peoria, Illinois, where he majored in teacher education. While in college, he faced discrimination, such as being kicked out of a local fast-food restaurant because of his vocal tics. However, his peers supported him by boycotting the restaurant, prompting the manager to issue an apology. Brad graduated cum laude with numerous academic honors. In the 1990s, Brad moved to Atlanta, Georgia, to pursue a teaching career. Despite his qualifications, he was rejected by 24 schools due to the challenges posed by his tics during interviews. Eventually, Mountain View Elementary School hired him to teach second and third grades. In 1997, he was honored with the Sallie Mae First Class Teacher of the Year Award. Currently, Brad teaches second grade at Tritt Elementary School in the suburbs of Atlanta. At the start of each school year, he educates his students about his Tourette syndrome to foster understanding and acceptance. Brad has been actively involved in various organizations. He has appeared in a public service announcement for the Tourette Syndrome Association and serves as the Vice President of the Tourette Syndrome Association of Georgia. He has also been a chairman for Relay for Life, a Little League coach, and even an MLB mascot. His contributions to the community have been widely recognized. In 2005, Brad co-authored his book, Front of the Class: How Tourette Syndrome Made Me the Teacher I Never Had, with Lisa Wysocky. The book won the Independent Publisher Book Award for Best Education Book of 2005. On May 26, 2006, Brad appeared on The Oprah Winfrey Show to share his inspiring story.
